topic: Thread Standard Behavior for Cross-Platform Design
explanation: Prior to C++11, writing multithreaded code required reliance on platform-specific APIs (like pthreads or Windows threads), making true cross-platform behavior difficult or impossible to guarantee. C++11 established concurrency not just through library primitives (threads, mutexes) but critically, through language constraints on compiler writers. This ensures that concurrent programs adhere to a single, standard memory model and behavior definition, providing a solid, reliable foundation for building portable concurrent software, regardless of the underlying operating system.
practical_example: A financial application team develops high-performance risk calculation software. By relying exclusively on `std::thread`, `std::mutex`, and `std::atomic`, they guarantee identical behavior and synchronization semantics when deploying the software on both Linux (using pthreads internally) and Windows (using its native thread API).
keywords: C++11 concurrency, standard memory model, cross-platform threading, C++ threads standardization
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
